tools.name: search_agents
tools.description: Search the curated Agent Switchboard directory of AI agents, MCP servers, and agentic tools. Filter by task, category slug, access methods, official (first-party listings from major vendors), verified, and/or auth type; sort by relevance, newest, most skills, or name. Verified: we checked it works —

tools.name: get_agent
tools.description: Full detail for one agent by slug: skills, auth, streaming/push support, tags, provider links, and useItNow: how to start using it (MCP client config, install command, API base URL, setup links). Verified: we checked it works — its URLs load and its declared access (API, MCP, CLI or extension) respo

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: All directory categories with live agent counts. Slugs are valid inputs for search_agents.

tools.name: compare_agents
tools.description: Put 2 or 3 listings side by side, as the site's /compare page does. For each listing: the facts that set it apart from the others ("Only one with a CLI", "No auth required", "Most skills (12)"). Then one row per field, with each listing's value by slug: what it is, provider, official vendor, verifie

tools.name: alternatives_to
tools.description: Listings that could stand in for one listing, strongest first, as on its /agents/<slug>/alternatives page. tools.name: connect_bundle
tools.description: One MCP client config to paste ({"mcpServers": …}, as Cursor and other MCP clients read it) for up to 10 listings, and how each one connects. A listing is in the config when its own docs give a hosted server address or a local command. An MCP server whose docs give neither comes with its setup guide

tools.name: submit_listing
tools.description: Suggest a new listing for the Agent Switchboard directory. This opens a PUBLIC GitHub issue that the maintainer reviews by hand; it does not publish anything. Use it only when the user asks to submit or list a product, after you show them the name, URL, and description you will send and they agree.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_agents, get_agent, submit_listing · Private data: search_agents, get_agent · Public sink: submit_listing.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_agents, get_agent, submit_listing · Private data: search_agents, get_agent · Public sink: submit_listing

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
